title: Training a Generalist Hallucination Detector across Multiple Domains via Adaptive Layer Aggregation

problem.claim: Hallucination detectors for large language models often degrade when evaluated under real-world domain shifts.

gap.claim: Existing work has underexplored layer-index shift, where the most informative internal layer varies across domains and fixed-layer detectors generalize poorly.

contributions.claim: The paper formalizes Multi-Domain Generalizable Hallucination Detection as training on multiple labeled domains and evaluating on unseen domains without test-domain supervision.
The paper proposes Stability-Aware Adaptive Layer Aggregation, which uses layer-wise instability estimates, per-layer projectors, invariant subspaces, and aggregation to build a robust detector.
The method provides an upper bound on the possible separability drop from training to an unseen test domain.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Stability-Aware Adaptive Layer Aggregation as a novel method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across four QA benchmarks and four LLaMA- and Qwen-family backbones ranging from 7B to 14B, the authors report that SALA achieves the best average performance among existing hallucination detection baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reliable hallucination detection is needed for deploying LLMs in safety-critical applications, but domain shifts reduce detector performance.
The paper defines multi-domain generalizable hallucination detection as cross-domain evaluation without test-domain supervision.
Layer-index shift causes fixed-layer detectors to generalize poorly because informative layers vary across domains.

SALA estimates layer instability, bounds separability drop, learns stable invariant subspaces, aggregates layers, and is reported to achieve the best average baseline performance across the stated benchmarks and backbones.

source_observation.claim: The most informative internal layer can vary substantially across domains, making fixed-layer detectors generalize poorly.

interpretation.claim: When internal representations shift across domains, adaptive multi-layer selection may be more robust than committing to one layer.

application.claim: For cross-domain detector design, measure layer stability on training domains and aggregate representations using stability-aware projectors.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond hallucination detection, the stated QA benchmarks, or the evaluated LLaMA and Qwen backbones.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, domain splits, evaluation metrics, baseline identities, or numerical performance results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the instability index, upper bound, projectors, or invariant-subspace learning.
The abstract does not report computational cost, ablations, or failure cases.
